context: The user asks for a number the evidence does not support and for a fix whose obvious forms all fail. Predicted baseline failure on the number: the agent repeats 0.941 to 0.844 as 9.7 points of lost quality, which the history file refutes — the dataset_version column shows three different case sets inside the window (v4.0.0, then v4.2.0 from 2026-08-14, then v4.4.0 from 2026-09-04), and docs/release-log.md records that each bump added and retired cases with no capture run made for either version, so the endpoints were never measured on the same suite. The defensible figure is the within-version arithmetic: about 2.2 points inside v4.0.0, 5.0 inside v4.2.0, 1.8 inside v4.4.0, with the two boundary steps uninterpretable. Predicted baseline failure on the fix: the agent guards the promotion step with if: success() and a branch condition and calls it done. The history refutes that too — all 42 nights were reported PASS, so a success guard would have promoted every one of them, and the anchor would have walked down exactly as it did. The second-most-likely non-fix is tightening MIN_RATIO, which the per-night numbers also rule out: the mean night-over-night step is about -0.24 points while ordinary nights already swing +0.3 and single legitimate nights fall 0.9. The real fix is an anchor that does not come from the job — a baseline committed to the repository, tied to a named release and the dataset version it was captured on — which the fixture blocks by other means too: the artifact carries retention-days 30, so the 2026-07-31 seed run is already unrecoverable, and the pull_request trigger lets a PR run overwrite the shared anchor.

checklist.name: MUST NOT anchor the gate to a run the job itself produced
checklist.description: MUST NOT deliver a gate that still compares each night against the previous night's output. The anchor becomes a baseline committed to the repository, tied to a named release and to the dataset version it was captured on. Adding if: success() or a branch guard to the promotion step, or keeping nightly promotion in any form while the comparison stays night-over-night, scores zero: every one of the 42 nights was reported PASS, so a success guard would have promoted all 42. Moving the anchor to a CI artifact that the job still rewrites, or leaving it on an artifact at all given retention-days 30, scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT quote 9.7 points as the quality loss
checklist.description: MUST NOT report 0.941 to 0.844 as 9.7 points of lost quality, even though the user asks for that number. The dataset version changed twice inside the window, so the endpoints sit on three different case sets. Full marks require the within-version figures instead — roughly 2.2 points inside v4.0.0, 5.0 inside v4.2.0, 1.8 inside v4.4.0 — together with the statement that the two version boundaries are not interpretable and that a real decline is nonetheless present inside every version. Handing back 9.7 points as the answer scores zero. Mentioning that the dataset changed without separating the within-version falls scores at most half.

checklist.name: Tightening the ratio rejected with the arithmetic
checklist.description: The postmortem states why raising MIN_RATIO cannot be the mechanism: the mean night-over-night step across the window is about -0.24 points, ordinary nights already move up to +0.3, and single legitimate nights fall as much as 0.9, so no night-over-night threshold separates six weeks of drift from one night of noise. Delivering a tightened MIN_RATIO as the fix scores zero. Rejecting it without the numbers from the history file scores at most half.

checklist.name: A dataset version bump forces a new anchor
checklist.description: The fix states that publishing a new dataset version requires capturing and committing a baseline on that version before the nightly job runs against it, so the anchor and the run are always on the same case set — the thing docs/release-log.md records was skipped for both v4.2.0 and v4.4.0. Absent, scores zero. Stated in prose but with nothing in the workflow or gate that enforces it scores at most half.

checklist.name: Pull-request runs cannot publish the anchor
checklist.description: The delivered workflow prevents a pull_request run from writing the shared baseline. A workflow that still promotes or uploads on any event scores zero.

checklist.name: Ownership of the anchor stated
checklist.description: The postmortem names who moves the baseline and on what event, so the anchor cannot advance as a side effect of a job running. Naming neither scores zero; naming an event but no owner scores at most half.

checklist.name: Suite green with new coverage
checklist.description: node --test passes, the shipped tests are kept or amended only where the new comparison makes an expectation obsolete, and at least one added test covers the new anchoring behaviour. A failing suite, or deleting the shipped tests outright, scores zero.

checklist.name: Postmortem delivered
checklist.description: docs/drift-postmortem.md exists and answers what the gate was measuring for six weeks. A document that only proposes a fix without answering that scores at most half.
